reviews.title: Great Compact Wooden Front Panel Case!!!
reviews.comment:
Stunning, especially for the price, sixty dollars for a tempered glass and wood front panel is a great deal. {HOWEVER DOES NOT SUPPORT 280mm AIO} my liquid freezer 2 does not fit with fans.
-The Glass side panel is magnetic with 2 inserts at the bottom to hook it, completely toolless design.
-2 mounts for 2.5” SSDs (thumb screws on bottom of case holding HDD/SSD cage).
-Super compact but long design for bigger GPUs
-LOTS of ventilation, 2 spots on the side of the case for 120mm fans and ventilation on both the PSU shroud and side of the PSU (this is great for the GPU!).
My only negatives are the lack of cable management (just enough but I’d leave the hdd tray in to prevent any wires from contacting the bottom front fan), lack of rubber grommets over cable holes and the plastic guides on the front panel. I’d be very gentle when prying from the bottom up and do it slowly, the problem is longevity, when you need to clean the mesh filter and break a plastic guide your kinda screwed, it’s really a simple fix to use aluminum and rubber like Corsair does. I’d recommend getting a portable air tool to clean it from the inside rather than take it off.
reviews.author: Gabriel

reviews.title: Good value for the price
reviews.comment: I picked up an old HP Omen 25L pre-built mATX on Facebook marketplace. Case was badly damaged and needed to be replaced. I was looking for something on the cheaper side when I came across this one. I was a bit skeptical, as it seemed like a generic fractal north. However, it did prove me wrong. It is a solid case that punches well above it's price. It has 3 preinstalled fans, however it looks like there is room for up to 10. The fans are a bit louder than more premium fans, but quieter than other cheaper fans. The sound profile really isn't bad either. If you are sensitive to fan noise, you may want to upgrade the fans, but this would increase the price of the case and may push you to something more premium. I myself am sensitive to fan noise, and I don't find them to be all that bad. The buttons being on the side is nice, as long as you have the PC on the right side of your desk. I was surprised that it included an optional speaker and a large amount of hardware.  It has room for a single 2.5" and a single 3.5" drive. Doesn't have as many features as some of the more expensive cases, however if you need a case on the simpler side to fit an ITX or mATX build, it is not a bad option at all.

reviews.title: Fit my use case!
reviews.comment: Case was perfect for my needs. I really needed the power button to be easily accessable from the side and the wood front panel goes great with my setup. One thing I would like to see implemented is cleaner screws. The motherboard screws I used had some grime on them from the factory. Not a huge deal, just would be a nice to have.
